run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/fraud-detection since 2026-11-18T02:09:16Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The RequestErrorRate alert for otel-demo/fraud-detection is explained by error status on fraud-detection's gRPC calls to the flagd feature-flag service: in the span-derived metric the only fraud-detection series carrying STATUS_CODE_ERROR are span_name=flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream and flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/ResolveInt, and the sampled traces show fraud-detection client spans on the EventStream operation with rpc.grpc.status_code=4 (DEADLINE_EXCEEDED) after ~594-602 s, with the paired flagd server span (v0.12.8) reporting otel.status_description "stream closed due to server-side timeout". The same EventStream failure pattern appears for the ad service, and flagd's pod is running/ready with 0 restarts, no CPU throttling and ~34 MB working set against a 512Mi limit, while every fault flag in the flagd-config ConfigMap is set to "off" - so neither a flagd pod failure, resource exhaustion nor an enabled flagd fault flag explains it. Kafka pod terminations exist but no fraud-detection error spans are on its Kafka operations. Because span-metric samples stop at 01:39:16 and the alert started at 02:09:16, and no pre-01:17 baseline exists (all pods were created 01:13-01:26), the trigger timing and whether the flagd stream timeout is a regression cannot be established; the conclusion is therefore partial.

claims.text: For service_name=fraud-detection, traces_span_metrics_calls_total exists with exactly six span_name/status_code series: flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream with STATUS_CODE_ERROR, flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/ResolveInt with STATUS_CODE_ERROR and STATUS_CODE_UNSET, resolve with STATUS_CODE_UNSET, orders receive with STATUS_CODE_UNSET and orders process with STATUS_CODE_UNSET.

The fraud-detection span counters first show STATUS_CODE_ERROR at 01:26:16 (value 1) and climb to 12 ERROR versus 449 UNSET spans at 01:31:16 and 12 ERROR versus 457 UNSET at 01:34:16 (about 2.6% error share); the last two points are 01:38:16 (12 ERROR / 457 UNSET) and 01:39:16 (5 ERROR / 25 UNSET, a counter reset), after which no span-metric samples exist.

Span metrics for all 15 service_name values (accounting, ad, cart, checkout, currency, email, fraud-detection, frontend, frontend-proxy, image-provider, payment, product-catalog, quote, recommendation, shipping) end at 01:39:16, so there are no traces_span_metrics_calls_total samples for any service between 01:39:16 and the query end 02:22:25.

In the sampled traces, 10 fraud-detection client spans on operation flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream carry error=true, otel.status_code=ERROR and rpc.grpc.status_code=4 (DEADLINE_EXCEEDED) with durations of 594.1-601.8 s, all starting between 01:17:53 and 01:19:41.

In trace bd06756e0c7d97b40a884e5dac7ffd05 the fraud-detection EventStream client span (span_id 98b55d8661c53e21, 599999905 us, rpc.grpc.status_code=4) has a child span at service flagd/service_version v0.12.8 (span_id 7a4ab60e782bfb14, CHILD_OF 98b55d8661c53e21) carrying error=true, rpc.grpc.status_code=4 and otel.status_description "stream closed due to server-side timeout" with duration 553397947 us; other flagd EventStream server spans on the same operation carry rpc.grpc.status_code=0 with durations 549-556 s.

The identical pattern is present for service ad: 10 ad client spans on flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream with error=true, rpc.grpc.status_code=4 and durations 596.9-604.2 s, paired with flagd server spans (v0.12.8) whose otel.status_description is "stream closed due to server-side timeout" (e.g. trace 3ed1b65c512ab69299434fbfe37f82ac).

Cumulative ERROR-status span counts in the same window exist for other services and operations too, including frontend GET /api/data (309), frontend grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds (309), frontend POST /api/checkout (77), ad flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/ResolveBoolean (21), ad EventStream (8), checkout oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder (13), recommendation /flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream (7) and shipping /get-quote (6); within fraud-detection the ERROR status appears only on the two flagd operations.

The flagd Deployment in otel-demo runs 1 requested / 1 ready replica with image ghcr.io/open-feature/flagd:v0.12.8 started as "flagd-build start --port 8013 --ofrep-port 8016 --uri file:./etc/flagd/demo.flagd.json", pod flagd-58db7486bd-2plsx is Running and ready with restartCount 0 (started 01:15:12) and no liveness/readiness probes defined.

The fraud-detection Deployment runs 10 requested / 10 ready replicas with image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-fraud-detection and env FLAGD_HOST=flagd, FLAGD_PORT=8013, KAFKA_ADDR=kafka:9092, OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT=http://otel-collector:4318 and a cpu limit of 100m; all 10 fraud-detection-9fb7d885b pods are Running and ready with restartCount 0, created between 01:14:55 and 01:16:23.

The flagd-config ConfigMap key demo.flagd.json defines the fault flags adFailure, adHighCpu, adManualGc, cartFailure, emailMemoryLeak, imageSlowLoad, kafkaQueueProblems, loadGeneratorFloodHomepage, paymentFailure, paymentUnreachable, productCatalogFailure and recommendationCacheFailure, and every one of them is in state ENABLED with defaultVariant "off" (i.e. no fault variant selected).

The otel-collector ConfigMap (key relay) defines a spanmetrics connector as a receiver of the traces pipeline and a "prometheus" exporter feeding the metrics pipeline, so the RequestErrorRate input metric traces_span_metrics_calls_total is generated from span statuses by the collector.
CPU CFS throttling at 01:34:16 is 0.030-0.229 of periods for fraud-detection pods and 0 for the flagd pod, compared with 0.062-0.318 for ad pods and 0.002-0.100 for frontend pods in the same reading.
The flagd container's maximum container_memory_working_set_bytes in the 15 minutes ending 01:44:16 was 34,258,944 bytes, far below its 512Mi limit and its GOMEMLIMIT of 60MiB.

Two Kafka pods in otel-demo have terminated containers with exitCode 1 and reason Error: kafka-ff7884766-vg9vr at 01:19:42 (restartCount 1) and kafka-ff7884766-lbw2w at 01:24:39 (restartCount 3); both are currently Running and ready.

Events inside the authorized window (01:28:35-01:32:48) contain no event involving flagd or fraud-detection; the groups are HorizontalPodAutoscaler FailedGetResourceMetric/FailedComputeMetricsReplicas (resource metrics API unavailable) and FailedGetScale for postgres, recommendation ScalingReplicaSet/SuccessfulRescale downscale events, and data-recorders Job/Pod/PersistentVolumeClaim events.

The cluster's namespaces are clickhouse, clickhouse-operator, default, ingress-nginx, kube-node-lease, kube-public, kube-system, metrics-server, opencost, opensearch, opentelemetry-collectors, opentelemetry-operator, otel-demo and prometheus; no chaos/fault-injection namespace is present.

flagd itself was not down or resource-starved during the window: its pod is Running and ready with 0 restarts, its CPU throttling ratio is 0 and its working set is ~34 MB against a 512Mi limit, so the stream closures cannot be attributed to a flagd crash, restart or resource exhaustion.

No flagd fault-injection setting is switched on: all twelve flags in flagd-config demo.flagd.json have defaultVariant "off", including kafkaQueueProblems and paymentFailure, so the fraud-detection error spans are not explained by an enabled flagd fault flag.

fraud-detection's error status is confined to flagd client operations: its Kafka consumer spans (orders receive, orders process) and its internal resolve span appear only with STATUS_CODE_UNSET, so the Kafka container terminations are not shown to produce this error rate.

Rejected: fraud-detection pods crashed, restarted or were evicted. All 10 fraud-detection-9fb7d885b pods are Running and ready with restartCount 0, no last-state termination and no Evicted/OOMKilled marks, and no pod events name them.

Rejected: CPU throttling of the fraud-detection pods caused the failed flagd streams. Their throttled-period fraction (0.030-0.229) is inside or below the range of ad pods (0.062-0.318), which show the same EventStream failures, while the flagd pod that closed the streams shows 0 throttling.

Rejected: the Kafka consumer path is the cause of the fraud-detection alert. Although kafka-ff7884766-vg9vr and kafka-ff7884766-lbw2w containers terminated with exitCode 1 (01:19:42 and 01:24:39), fraud-detection's Kafka consumer spans carry no ERROR status and its only ERROR series are the two flagd operations.

The errors that trip RequestErrorRate originate in the flagd streaming connection rather than in fraud-detection's business logic: each fraud-detection pod's flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream call was terminated by flagd with "stream closed due to server-side timeout" (child flagd span, rpc.grpc.status_code=4) and the client span then ended as DEADLINE_EXCEEDED after ~600 s; the same sequence is visible for the ad service, so it is shared flagd streaming behaviour.

The error burst may be a bring-up/stream-lifecycle artifact rather than an ongoing fault: all demo pods were created 01:13-01:26, the failed EventStream calls started 01:17:53-01:19:41 (shortly after the pods started) and ended ~01:27:53-01:29:41, and no second wave of EventStream errors is visible before telemetry stops at 01:39:16.

The state that made the alert fire at 02:09:16 cannot be verified from this telemetry: the span-derived error ratio was already elevated (~2.6%) at 01:31-01:38, before the alert start, and the span-metric series stop at 01:39:16, so a later signal driving the alert onset cannot be observed.

Compare RequestErrorRate for the other flagd clients (ad and recommendation both show EventStream ERROR spans and recall/ResolveBoolean errors) and, if the same pattern fires there, treat the ~600 s streaming RPC as shared infrastructure noise instead of a per-service fault.

Review flagd's gRPC stream timeout/keepalive settings against the ~600 s client deadline (flagd is started with only --port, --ofrep-port and --uri, so no timeout is configured explicitly) and consider excluding long-lived streaming operations such as flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream from any error-rate ratio that treats status 4 on a stream as a request failure.

Investigate the telemetry gap and the alert rule itself: span-metric samples for all services stop at 01:39:16 while the alert is dated 02:09:16, so check Prometheus/otel-collector scrape and export health after 01:39 and retrieve the RequestErrorRate rule expression to confirm which metric, ratio and window produced 0.02222222222222222.

gaps: No baseline before 01:17:53 exists: every otel-demo pod was created 01:13-01:26 and span metrics only start ~01:26, so it cannot be determined whether the flagd EventStream timeouts are new or routine.

Application logs are unavailable for this run: fetch_pod_logs for fraud-detection-9fb7d885b-2m24l and flagd-58db7486bd-2plsx returned 0 lines (all streams status "read"), and otel-collector-564d9c7987-bln8k returned 0 lines for the error filter, so the container-side messages behind the spans are unknown.

The RequestErrorRate alert rule could not be read: list_prometheus_rules for rule_name RequestErrorRate and for {severity="warning"} returned no data, so the exact metric, ratio and evaluation window behind 0.02222222222222222 are unknown.

Telemetry after 01:39:16 (span metrics) and after ~01:44:16 (container metrics) is absent, so the state at the alert start 02:09:16 is unknown; the reported 2.22% cannot be reproduced from available data (the last visible fraud-detection reading at 01:34:16 is 12 ERROR / 457 UNSET).

The flagd-side reason for the server-side stream timeout is not observable: flagd logs are empty, no flagd configuration value for a stream/keepalive timeout was found, and flagd pod state is healthy, so why flagd closes streams after ~530-556 s is unknown.

Details of the flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/ResolveInt error spans for fraud-detection are unknown: the span-metric series shows STATUS_CODE_ERROR but no matching trace was returned by traces_search_by_tags, and which flag or gRPC status is involved is not visible.

No kube-state-metrics series (kube_deployment_status_*, kube_pod_owner, kube_replicaset_owner) were returned by get_metric_names and kube_deployment_status_replicas_ready returned no data, so workload state was taken from the Kubernetes API at query time only, not from history.

Two Kafka containers terminated with exitCode 1 (reason Error) at 01:19:42 and 01:24:39; their container logs and the message that killed them were not read, so this event remains unexplained and unlinked to any observed request failure.
next_steps: Retrieve the RequestErrorRate Prometheus rule (metric, ratio, window, for clause) and its evaluation history to confirm that the fired value came from fraud-detection's flagd EventStream ERROR spans and to see which evaluation was current at 02:09:16.

Check flagd gRPC streaming configuration/version behaviour (v0.12.8) for the server-side stream timeout that closes flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream at ~530-556 s while clients wait up to ~600 s, and compare with the other flagd clients (ad, recommendation, checkout, cart, currency, email, payment, product-catalog, quote, shipping).

Investigate why span-metric and container-metric samples stop at 01:39:16/~01:44:16 (otel-collector metrics pipeline, Prometheus scrape of otel-collector:8889) before concluding anything about service health after that time.

Read the two terminated Kafka containers' previous logs (kafka-ff7884766-vg9vr, kafka-ff7884766-lbw2w) to determine whether those exitCode 1 terminations relate to any consumer-side errors, even though no fraud-detection Kafka error spans were observed.

view.series_note: traces_span_metrics_calls_total counts spans of every operation of the service (internal, client and server spans alike), summed over the labels kept in this query; it is not a count of requests. status_code STATUS_CODE_UNSET means the span carried no status; it does not mean the call succeeded.

view.cannot_prove: Objects are the cluster's state when the query ran, not during the incident window: they cannot prove what was true earlier, and an object missing now may have existed then. Events cover only their own timestamps inside the window; an event that is not returned is unknown, not proof nothing happened (events expire and timestamps are often null). <none> means the path reached no value in that object, not that the field is absent from the kind; a filtered table is not a full picture of the kind.

content.name: otel-collector
content.relay:
connectors:
  spanmetrics:
    dimensions:
    - default: otel-demo
      name: namespace
exporters:
  clickhouse:
    endpoint: http://clickhouse-clickhouse.clickhouse.svc.cluster.local:8123
    logs_table_name: otel_demo_logs
    password: ""
    traces_table_name: otel_demo_traces
    username: default
  debug: {}
  opensearch:
    http:
      endpoint: http://opensearch-master.opensearch.svc.cluster.local:9200
      tls:
        insecure: true
    logs_index: otel-logs
    logs_index_time_format: yyyy-MM-dd
  otlp:
    endpoint: jaeger-collector.opentelemetry-collectors.svc.cluster.local:4317
    tls:
      insecure: true
  otlphttp/prometheus:
    endpoint: http://prometheus-kube-prometheus-prometheus.prometheus.svc.cluster.local:9090
    tls:
      insecure: true
  prometheus:
    endpoint: 0.0.0.0:8889
extensions:
  health_check:
    endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:13133
processors:
  batch: {}
  k8sattributes:
    extract:
      metadata:
      - k8s.namespace.name
      - k8s.deployment.name
      - k8s.statefulset.name
      - k8s.daemonset.name
      - k8s.cronjob.name
      - k8s.job.name
      - k8s.node.name
      - k8s.pod.name
      - k8s.pod.uid
      - k8s.pod.start_time
    passthrough: false
    pod_association:
    - sources:
      - from: resource_attribute
        name: k8s.pod.ip
    - sources:
      - from: resource_attribute
        name: k8s.pod.uid
    - sources:
      - from: connection
  memory_limiter:
    check_interval: 5s
    limit_percentage: 80
    spike_limit_percentage: 25
  resource:
    attributes:
    - action: insert
      from_attribute: k8s.pod.uid
      key: service.instance.id
  resourcedetection:
    detectors:
    - env
    - system
  transform:
    error_mode: ignore
    trace_statements:
    - context: span
      statements:
      - replace_pattern(name, "\\?.*", "")
      - replace_match(name, "GET /api/products/*", "GET /api/products/{productId}")
receivers:
  httpcheck/frontend-proxy:
    targets:
    - endpoint: http://frontend-proxy:8080
  jaeger:
    protocols:
      grpc:
        endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:14250
      thrift_compact:
        endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:6831
      thrift_http:
        endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:14268
  nginx:
    collection_interval: 10s
    endpoint: http://image-provider:8081/status
  otlp:
    protocols:
      grpc:
        endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:4317
      http:
        cors:
          allowed_origins:
          - http://*
          - https://*
        endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:4318
  postgresql:
    endpoint: postgresql:5432
    metrics:
      postgresql.blks_hit:
        enabled: true
      postgresql.blks_read:
        enabled: true
      postgresql.deadlocks:
        enabled: true
      postgresql.tup_deleted:
        enabled: true
      postgresql.tup_fetched:
        enabled: true
      postgresql.tup_inserted:
        enabled: true
      postgresql.tup_returned:
        enabled: true
      postgresql.tup_updated:
        enabled: true
    password: [REDACTED_CREDENTIAL]
    tls:
      insecure: true
    username: root
  prometheus:
    config:
      scrape_configs:
      - job_name: opentelemetry-collector
        scrape_interval: 10s
        static_configs:
        - targets:
          - ${env:MY_POD_IP}:8888
  redis:
    collection_interval: 10s
    endpoint: valkey-cart:6379
    username: valkey
  zipkin:
    endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:9411
service:
  extensions:
  - health_check
  pipelines:
    logs:
      exporters:
      - clickhouse
      - debug
      processors:
      - k8sattributes
      - memory_limiter
      - resourcedetection
      - resource
      - batch
      receivers:
      - otlp
    metrics:
      exporters:
      - debug
      - prometheus
      processors:
      - k8sattributes
      - memory_limiter
      - resourcedetection
      - resource
      - batch
      receivers:
      - httpcheck/frontend-proxy
      - nginx
      - otlp
      - postgresql
      - redis
      - spanmetrics
    traces:
      exporters:
      - clickhouse
      - debug
      - otlp
      - spanmetrics
      processors:
      - k8sattributes
      - memory_limiter
      - resourcedetection
      - resource
      - transform
      - batch
      receivers:
      - otlp
      - jaeger
      - zipkin
  telemetry:
    metrics:
      level: detailed
      readers:
      - pull:
          exporter:
            prometheus:
              host: 0.0.0.0
              port: 8888
